1 big thing: Meta's AI app takes off
 
Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Stock: Getty Images

Meta's Muse is rocketing up the app charts with a distinctly practical vision for AI — an agent that can shop, haggle, cancel subscriptions and clear away the digital drudgery of everyday life, Axios' Zachary Basu writes.

  • Mark Zuckerberg is staking Meta's AI comeback on one of the enduring strengths of his internet empire: making new technology feel native to billions of ordinary people.

🤳 Ten days after launch, Muse is the No. 1 free iPhone app in America — ahead of ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Instagram.

  • Muse pairs a highly polished interface — built around a cuddly, customizable avatar — with serious computing power, including its own secure virtual computer and browser in the cloud.
  • Users give it tasks in plain English, while Muse itself surfaces ideas, goals and suggestions that teach people about its capabilities as it works across websites and connected accounts.

🤖 Muse poses an early test of whether Meta's structural advantages — product design, distribution and an intimate grasp of consumer behavior — can shape the AI race more than raw intelligence alone.

🤔 Reality check: The more useful Muse becomes, the more of your life it needs to see: email, calendars, financial accounts, purchases, contacts and eventually even the phone calls it can make in your name.

  • Zuckerberg has repeatedly tried to reinvent both Meta and himself, from Facebook founder to metaverse evangelist to AI optimist. A deep reservoir of public distrust has proven far harder to shed.

2. 🏦 End of an era at Berkshire
 
Warren Buffett cheers as he and Hillary Clinton arrive at a rally in Omaha, Neb., in 2016. Photo: Andrew Harnik/AP

Warren Buffett stepped down today as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway after more than six decades, Axios' Dan Primack writes.

  • It's the end of an extraordinary era, unlikely to ever be matched.

🪑 Buffett, who turned over the CEO reins at the end of 2025 to Greg Abel, will become chairman emeritus and remain a director.

  • He said in a statement: "Father Time always wins. He has, however, been generous with me. He has given me the opportunity to see Berkshire reach a point where I am more confident than ever about what lies ahead."

4. 🐈 1 science thing: New cat dropped
 
Photo: Fernando Faciole/National Geographic via Reuters

Meet Leopardus tilcayo — the first newly identified cat species in over a century, according to a new study.

  • The wild cat, a bit smaller than a housecat, lives in Bolivia's cloud forest. Locals call it simply "Tilcayo."

🌲 National Geographic on the discovery's importance: "The new paper doesn't just name a new species; it redraws the cat family tree to have a lot more branches than previously thought."

  • "What's more, the researchers hope the methods used to identify L. tilcayo may soon be used to find even more cat species spread across the world, and even transform how we protect them."
